technical-summary: Fixed provider CLI probes failing with WinError 2 on Windows. Root cause: probes ran a bare argv list (subprocess.run(["opencode","--version"])) which CreateProcess cannot use to launch npm/pip .CMD shims. Added shared adapters/probe.py with run_cli() (shell-routes on Windows, direct exec on POSIX) and probe_cli_version() (which-resolve + run + correct available flag). Refactored opencode and openhands probes to use probe_cli_version (also fixed their except handler that returned available=True on failure). Routed copilot, qwen, and roo subprocess calls through run_cli (preserving their present-on-PATH availability semantics). Added regression tests covering missing executable, spawn failure -> available False, success/nonzero exit, cross-platform run_cli, a win32-only .CMD shim test proving bare list fails while run_cli succeeds, and opencode delegation to the shared helper. All 7 new tests + existing provider unit suite pass; ruff clean.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed provider CLIs (opencode and others) reporting WinError 2 on Windows by running their version probes through the shell so npm-installed .CMD shims resolve correctly.

technical-summary: Validated all providers in Docker and added a cross-provider probe contract test. Ran tests/dev/run_provider_cli_isolated.py (bind-mounted) across all 12 installable providers in isolated Linux containers: every provider passed real install/health/uninstall (plandex brew roundtrip skipped per harness.yaml policy; no failures). Confirmed the default probe _probe_cli (registry.py) resolves the full executable via shutil.which before running, so it is unaffected by the Windows .CMD bug; the continue and pi custom probes do not spawn subprocess (which-check / file-check). Added tests/unit/providers/test_provider_probe_contract.py: parametrized over every PATH-based provider probe, stubs shutil.which to None and asserts _probe_provider_cli returns available=False with executable=None — guarding the whole class of bug (probe crash or masking failure as available) across all providers on any platform. 14 tests pass; full provider unit suite green; ruff clean.
user-summary-candidate: Verified every provider installs and runs correctly in Docker, and added a test ensuring no provider's availability check crashes or falsely reports installed when its CLI is missing.

technical-summary: Added async enable_language() to lsp_api: enables a language in lsp.json then resolves and installs that language's missing server dependencies in one step, with atomic rollback (removes the language) if the install fails for a newly added language. lsp_add_language MCP tool is now async and routes through enable_language with run_blocking_with_output, so the client only names the language (no dependency-id knowledge required). Also fixed resolve_project_root to stop the upward project-marker walk at the user home directory (Path.home()) so paths beneath home (e.g. tmp/AppData dirs) no longer inherit home's LSP config. Added two unit tests (install-then-enable success, rollback-on-install-failure) and the home-boundary fix repaired a previously env-dependent failing config test. Verified end-to-end: real enable_language('python') ran uv tool install pyright (pyright 1.1.410), pyright-langserver landed on PATH, config_status reported binary_available, and pyright booted returning 160 document symbols.
user-summary-candidate: Enabling a language LSP now installs its language server automatically in one step — you just name the language (e.g. python) and the matching server binary is resolved and installed for you, with rollback if the install fails. Also fixed project-root detection to stop at your home folder so temp/working dirs no longer pick up home's LSP config.

technical-summary: Wired pi-lens LSP support into the coding-lsp enable flow. Added an optional on_lsp_enabled hook to ProviderDescriptor: a provider-declared capability fired when coding-lsp is enabled so the provider can provision its own LSP support. coding_lsp_bootstrap._on_enabled now calls a new language_servers_sync.provision_provider_lsp_support() that fans out to each descriptor's on_lsp_enabled (best-effort, failures logged not fatal). The pi adapter implements _pi_ensure_lens, which runs `<pi-bin> install npm:pi-lens` via resolve_agent_bin (skips if the pi harness is absent, idempotent). pi-lens auto-discovers language servers from PATH, so no per-language config writer is needed — the server binaries installed by enable_language are sufficient. Providers that self-provide LSP (language_servers_config OR on_lsp_enabled set) are now excluded from the generic ag-lsp MCP projection in sync_generic_lsp_mcp_to_providers, so pi gets pi-lens instead of the redundant ag-lsp MCP server (and any previously-synced ag-lsp entry is pruned). Added 5 unit tests covering the pi hook (skip/install paths), generic-MCP exclusion of self-LSP providers, and provisioning fan-out. Decision: provisioning fires on COMPONENT_ENABLED only (consistent with existing enable-time provider sync), not on install.
user-summary-candidate: When the coding-lsp component is enabled, the pi agent now automatically installs the pi-lens extension, which auto-discovers your installed language servers from PATH — so enabling a language (which installs its server) just works in pi with no extra setup. pi uses pi-lens for code intelligence instead of the generic LSP bridge.

technical-summary: Fixed opencode LSP key mismatch. coding-lsp's sync is language-keyed (e.g. 'python'), but opencode keys its lsp object by its own built-in server name ('pyright' for Python, 'clangd' for C++; 'typescript'/'rust' already match the language id). Kept coding-lsp generic and moved the mapping into the opencode adapter: added _LANGUAGE_TO_OPENCODE_KEY ({python: pyright, cpp: clangd}) plus _to_opencode_key/_to_language helpers. write_language_servers_opencode now writes under the opencode key, remove_language_servers_opencode resolves the language id to the opencode key before deleting, and read_language_servers_opencode maps opencode keys back to our language ids (languages absent from the map pass through unchanged). Without this, syncing Python produced a stray lsp.python entry instead of configuring opencode's built-in pyright server. Updated the opencode roundtrip test and added cpp->clangd mapping and typescript passthrough tests. Built-in keys confirmed from opencode docs. Follow-up to verify: whether the codex adapter ([language_servers.<name>]) needs the same internal mapping.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed opencode language-server config: Python now correctly configures opencode's built-in 'pyright' server (and C++ its 'clangd' server) instead of creating a mismatched 'python' entry. The LSP component stays language-agnostic; the opencode adapter maps to opencode's server names internally.

technical-summary: Surface lifecycle observer (_on_component_lifecycle) only branched on lifecycle.component.installed/uninstalled; the disabled and enabled events fired by disable_component/enable_component fell through silently, so disabling a component never pruned its managed surface blocks from instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, QWEN.md, COPILOT.md, .clinerules, .roo). Mapped enabled->apply and disabled->prune+apply, paralleling installed/uninstalled. Root cause was masked because the integration suite (test_provider_surface_lifecycle.py) calls prune/apply directly to compensate for the absent event bus in test isolation, never exercising the observer event->action mapping. Added test_surface_observer_wiring.py covering all four lifecycle events plus the non-Path project_root guard.
user-summary-candidate: Disabling a component now removes its instruction blocks (e.g. ag-* tag doctrine) from AGENTS.md and other provider files, instead of leaving them stranded until uninstall.

technical-summary: Removed the redundant coding-lsp/usage surface contribution that duplicated the ag-lsp MCP tool list (lsp_symbols, lsp_diagnostics, etc.) into every provider's instruction file. The block was surfaced unconditionally to all providers, but the ag-lsp MCP server is only propagated to providers that don't self-provide LSP (opencode via native pyright language_servers_config, pi via on_lsp_enabled/pi-lens). This caused opencode's AGENTS.md to advertise lsp_* tools the agent didn't actually have, so the agent hunted for them, failed, and fell back to running pyright CLI. Root-cause fix: delete the contribution so the MCP registration is the single source of truth for tool availability — MCP delivers tool names and descriptions to the agent automatically via tools/list, and only to providers that actually receive the server. Usage doctrine remains in each MCP server's instructions field in coding-lsp.yaml. Regenerated provider surfaces (skill_surfaces apply), which pruned the coding-lsp/usage block from AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and GEMINI.md. No gating mechanism and no native-LSP instruction block were added (chosen approach: omit). Providers unit suite green. Follow-up (not done): the ag-lsp-mgmt harness-instructions block is the same class of MCP-tool duplication and could be reconsidered; and lsp_mcp.py's FastMCP server does not currently pass the coding-lsp.yaml ag-lsp instructions field as server-level instructions.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed agents being told to use LSP tools (lsp_diagnostics, lsp_symbols) that aren't available to them. The LSP tool list is no longer duplicated into instruction files (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md); agents discover LSP tools directly from the MCP server, so only agents that actually have the LSP server see those tools.

technical-summary: Replaced the per-block managed-surface fences with a single regenerated managed region per file. Previously each contribution was wrapped in its own <!-- AUDIAGENTIC:BEGIN <id> -->...<!-- AUDIAGENTIC:END <id> --> comment pair and matched/pruned by id. Now all of a file's managed blocks live inside one invisible boundary pair (<!-- ag:managed:begin -->...<!-- ag:managed:end -->) containing friendly `## Title` headings and a one-line managed notice; the region is regenerated wholesale on each apply. base.py: removed managed_block + prune_managed_blocks; added MANAGED_REGION_BEGIN/END/NOTICE constants, _REGION_RE, _LEGACY_BLOCK_RE, strip_managed_content(), render_managed_region(), and rewrote apply_managed_blocks() to strip prior region + legacy fences (auto-migration) then append the regenerated region (empty blocks remove the region). manager.py: prune_provider_surfaces now groups active blocks by path and calls apply_managed_blocks (region regeneration) instead of id-based prune_managed_blocks, so removed contributions drop out and files that lose all contributions are cleaned; dropped the prune_managed_blocks import. Block identity (block_id) is retained in the in-memory SurfaceBlock model (dedup, plan reporting) but is no longer emitted into files. Updated unit tests (region replacement, empty-removal, legacy migration, prune) and the consistency test (region regex + single-well-formed-region check + legacy-absence). Updated the Docker-gated integration helper managed_blocks_in to map region `## Title` headings back to contribution ids via load_surface_contributions. Regenerated all tracked agent surface files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, COPILOT.md, GEMINI.md, QWEN.md, .clinerules/audiagentic.md, .roo/rules/audiagentic.md) to the new region layout. Behavior note: managed content now consolidates into one contiguous region (moved to end of user-owned files on migration) rather than interleaving. Full unit suite passes.
user-summary-candidate: Managed sections in agent instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, etc.) are now wrapped in a single clean region with readable `## Title` headings and a 'managed by AUDiaGentic' notice, instead of noisy per-block <!-- AUDIAGENTIC:BEGIN/END --> comments around every entry. Old files migrate automatically on the next surface apply.

technical-summary: Generic component-driven lifecycle for generated per-tag skill files. Added owner_component_id to ActionDescriptor, set by the tag loader from the component whose config declares the action. New contributions.active_tag_ids(project_root) returns tags whose owning component is installed+enabled (None=all; empty owner treated active); load_tag_surface_contributions uses it instead of the hardcoded agent-jobs gate (behaviour-identical today as all tags are agent-jobs-owned). prune_provider_surfaces now deletes generated skill_surface_path files for inactive tags across all providers (.agents/.claude/.clinerules/.opencode/.gemini), removes emptied per-tag dirs, and returns a new deleted list - these whole managed files have no region for the rewrite path to strip. skill_surfaces._load_skills_from_registry skips inactive tags so regeneration cannot resurrect pruned skills. Added test_skill_lifecycle.py covering owner filtering, prune deletion/retention, and generation gating. Live cleanup removed 15 orphaned ag-* skill files left by the disabled agent-jobs component; .audiagentic/skills override sources untouched.
user-summary-candidate: Disabling or uninstalling a component that contributes workflow tags now removes its generated skill/command files from every provider (Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Cline, Gemini), not just the doctrine blocks - and they return on re-enable.
